meta.week_label: Week of Oct 29 - Nov 2, 2026 (Yahoo Week 9, BTO Week 9, NFL Week 8)
calibration: Backtest 2026 wks 1-8 (444 games): picks rated 60-70% hit 65%, 70-80% hit 70%, 80-90% hit 83%, 90%+ hit 86%.
Straight-up: model 70% vs market 75%; model trails early weeks, near market by wks 6-8.
Market lines: ESPN DraftKings Sat 08:07 AM CT for 47 games; CFBD consensus for the rest.

cards.title: CFP 2026 points pool

rows.why: Pool line a point better than market; Utah run game #4
rows.was: not on last card; dropped Oregon -3.5

rows.why: Pool +13.5 is 2 pts better than market +11.5

notes: Why Utah -6.5 (cover 55%): the pool line is a point better than the market (-7.5) and crosses 7. Utah's offense (#6) and run game (#4) face Cincinnati's defense (#97) and run defense (#100). Cincinnati ruled out its starting center Friday.

Why Auburn +13.5 (cover 53%): the pool line is 2 points better than the market (+11.5), the stale-line edge that covered about 61% in the backtest. Auburn's run game (#25) meets Ole Miss's run defense (#87), and Ole Miss's lead RB Kewan Lacy is out. Our stats lean Ole Miss slightly, so this rests on the line.

Why not Oregon -3.5: elite defense (#5), but the offense is #48 with a backup QB, Oregon lost 2 of its last 3 (15, 17 and 10 points), and the market moved 2 points toward Northwestern. Its edge was stats only, which the backtest says doesn't beat the market.
Sizing by expected payout (top 12 paid, $1,015 to $44 from a $2,900 pot): splitting all 11,904 over 2 bets ≈ $63 expected and a 24% chance of a paid finish; all-in on one game ≈ $40 and 15%.
Rebuy: worth the $25 if both lose (about 1 in 5). Last chance is this week (none after 11am Nov 7).
Also worth a look: Wake Forest -12.5 (53%). Tap any game in All pool games for its full breakdown. Pool locks Sat 11am CT.
